content: The roots of education and self-discipline are bitter, but the fruit is sweet and eternal.
author: Ancient Greek Proverbs
sourceWork: Tas men rizas pikras, tous de karpous glykeis — Isocrates & Aristotle
explanation: Sitting in study while others play, sweating in the gym while others feast, and mastering your emotions while others indulge is demanding and uncomfortable. But that initial bitterness is the root; once the tree matures, you feast on the sweet fruit of sovereign mastery and peace.
practicalInsight: Embrace the discomfort of your training or study today, keeping your eyes fixed on the sweet fruit of mastery.
reflectionPrompt: What worthwhile discipline are you avoiding because you are unwilling to taste the initial bitterness of the root?
